issue.description:
Set up test framework to exercise capability absence/presence between the two binaries

Acceptance:
- Create test harness that can run both binary variants
- Add tests for attempt-resolution capability detection
- Add tests for graceful degradation when capability missing
- Add tests for proper feature flag handling
- Tests should pass with pre-feature binary (capability absent)
- Tests should pass with feature-enabled binary (capability present)
issue.notes:
Delivered: capability detection test framework that runs both binary variants, committed and pushed as dbe508c (c6f99af..dbe508c on main, Forgejo origin).

Framework (tests/capability_framework.rs):
- BinaryHarness::with_binary(path) runs the same test body against an explicit binary instead of the hardcoded cargo-built bead (all prior methods routed through it; existing tests unchanged and passing)
- pinned_variant(role)/verified_pinned_variant(role) locate pins by role through pinned-binaries/commits.json and verify each pin's embedded --version against its *.metadata.json before use
- capabilities_of()/version_of() probe a bare binary outside any workspace (/var/tmp scratch); unrecognized_subcommand() captures clap's clean degradation signal

Matrix (tests/capability_variant_matrix.rs, 11 tests, all #[serial]):
- attempt-resolution capability detection: feature-enabled pin advertises attempt_outcome (supported, 5 outcomes, 5 actions, replay/revision/fencing/evidence flags, receipt+request schema refs), resolve command, and attempt-outcome/resolve-receipt/resolve-request schemas; pre-feature pin omits all of them while keeping the core 10-command surface
- graceful degradation: on the pre-feature 0.2.4 baseline, resolve exits 2 with clap 'unrecognized subcommand', no panic, and init/create/list still work on the same binary
- feature flag handling: Cargo.toml declares attempt-resolution non-default, and a flag-off build advertises the same attempt_outcome shape as the flag-on pin (the flag is a documented empty marker)
- consumer contract: capability document predicts live command surface on BOTH variants (attempt_outcome present <=> resolve invocable)

Key finding encoded in test docs: the cargo attempt-resolution flag gates no code; the functional 'capability absent' variant is the pinned 0.2.4 tree (bead-pre-feature), not a flag-off build.

Verification: cargo test --test capability_variant_matrix --test capability_framework --test pinned_binary_capability => 16+5+15 all passed (0.13s/0.53s/0.63s); rustfmt --edition 2024 --check clean; cargo clippy on all three targets clean. Both pinned binaries verified live against their recorded metadata versions during the run.

RE-VERIFICATION 2026-09-03 (re-dispatch after the 16:48Z gate reopen, failure-count:1): the framework is delivered and green at current HEAD ab1e0b2 (== origin/main). A sibling dispatch on this same bead pushed ab1e0b2 (16:39Z), a rewrite/extension of the same two files — the matrix description above reflects the dbe508c shape; at ab1e0b2 tests/capability_variant_matrix.rs carries 6 matrix tests (variant_pair_resolves_as_distinct_verified_binaries, capability_detection_matches_each_variant, capability_absence_degrades_gracefully, capability_presence_exposes_full_surface, feature_flag_handling_is_decoupled_from_capability, variants_share_the_core_contract) driving the same verified pins. - harness runs both binary variants: BinaryHarness::with_binary + capability_variant_pair() — registry-resolved by role from pinned-binaries/commits.json, --version provenance-checked and sha256 byte-checked against metadata, asserted genuinely distinct

issue.description:
## Outcome
`bead init` run in a directory *below* an existing bead-rs workspace never
exits 0 having silently adopted that ancestor. It fails closed, naming the
enclosing workspace, and creates a separate workspace in the current
directory only when `--nested` is passed. Its help text ("Initialize a new
bead workspace in the current directory") then matches its behaviour.
Decision: fail closed rather than nest implicitly. Implicit nesting would
split a repo's store whenever init is run from a subdirectory, the same
silent-misrouting class that R030 refuses for foreign `.beads`. Goal: Profile. This is step 4 of the
public NEEDLE README quickstart (`cd <your-repo> && ... bead init --prefix <name>`),
which strangers run against the public bead-rs release.

Work on this issue directly. Do not create sub-issues, do not split this work,
and do not decompose it into smaller tasks.

## Current state (evidence)
Observed 2026-10-26 with the published bead 0.2.6 during a NEEDLE stranger
test. The project was a fresh `git init` repo at
`/home/coding/scratch/needle-stranger.X/proj`, and `/home/coding/scratch/.beads`
already existed (a smoke-test store):

    $ bead init --prefix quickstart
    Workspace already exists at: /data/build/scratch
    Prefix: bead
    UUID: 21a9e91e-...
    Schema up to date (version 22)          # exit 0
    $ bead create --title 'Add a CONTRIBUTING.md ...' --priority 2
    bead-fbc07f04                           # written into the ancestor's store

The requested prefix was ignored, migrations ran against the ancestor's
database, and the bead landed in an unrelated workspace (bead-fbc07f04 was
closed afterwards as a test artifact).

Cause, at origin/main dd79a2d0: `cmd_init` (src/main.rs ~1320) calls
`store::WorkspaceConfig::probe()` (src/store/mod.rs:156-188). probe walks up
from cwd and returns `Ready` for the first ancestor `.beads/config.json`, and
`cmd_init` treats `Ready` as "already exists".

## Scoped work
- `cmd_init`: when probe returns `Ready` and the workspace root is not the
  current directory, do not touch the ancestor (no migrations, no writes)
  and exit with the conflict code (4). The message names the ancestor root,
  says that `bead init` at that root reuses it, and says that
  `bead init --nested` creates a separate workspace here.
- New `--nested` flag on `init`: initialize at the current directory via the
  same path as `NotFound`. Document it in `bead init --help`.
- Unchanged: re-init at the workspace root itself (idempotent, applies
  pending migrations), the `Uninitialized` rebuild, and the R030 refusal
  for a foreign `.beads`.
- Tests in tests/cli_init.rs: (a) nested init without the flag exits 4,
  stderr names the outer root, and the outer store's issue count and
  schema are unchanged; (b) `--nested` creates `<nested>/.beads/config.json`
  with the requested prefix; (c) re-init at the root still exits 0.

## Acceptance (a worker can run these)
- `cargo test --test cli_init` passes, including the new nested-init test.
- `cargo check --all-targets --quiet` (the workspace gate) passes.
- Throwaway check with the built binary: `T=$(mktemp -d /tmp/b1.XXXXXX)`;
  `bead init --prefix outer` in `$T`; `mkdir "$T/inner"`; then
  `bead init --prefix inner` in `$T/inner` exits 4 naming `$T`, and
  `bead init --prefix inner --nested` exits 0 printing `Root: $T/inner`.
  Afterwards `rm -rf "$T"`.
- Pushed commit on main of jedarden/bead-rs (Forgejo origin).

## Out of scope
- Changing discovery for any command other than `init`.
- NEEDLE docs/README changes (NEEDLE's quickstart runs init at the repo root).
- The `--skip-foreign-workspace` semantics.
- Cutting a bead-rs release.
issue.notes:
Delivered on main (Forgejo origin), all pushed:
- 3e81ddfb: cmd_init fails closed when discovery finds a Ready workspace ABOVE cwd - Error::conflict -> exit 4, message names the ancestor root and both remedies (re-run init at that root / init --nested here), ancestor untouched (no migrations, no repairs, no writes). New --nested flag initializes in cwd via the same path as NotFound; init --help documents it. Re-init at the workspace root (idempotent + pending migrations), the Uninitialized rebuild, and the R030 foreign-.beads refusals unchanged. Three new cli_init tests (fail-closed below workspace incl. ancestor-store-untouched assertions, --nested separate workspace with store-separation assertion, root re-init with a nested child present); the file moved to a .beads-free tempdir base. NOTE: this commit also carried an unrelated staged hunk (cmd_sync_status checkpoint_git_conflict reporting) from concurrent shared-tree work; it compiles (cargo check --all-targets green) - flagged here for the owning thread.
- b6d02326: rustfmt follow-up for the concurrency suite.
- 31c63c0e: concurrency_recovery_variants scratch_dir picks a .beads-free tempdir base (clean_beads_free_base, mirroring cli_init temp_workspace_dir) so the new fail-closed refusal cannot redden that suite on hosts carrying a stray /var/tmp/.beads.

Verification (own git-archive extraction of the final tree, hardlink-seeded target /data/build/bead-rs/gates/e4acee24-r9; extraction byte-identical to 31c63c0e on all build inputs):
- cargo test --test cli_init: exit 0, 22 passed / 0 failed, fresh Compiling line; all three nested tests ok.
- cargo check --all-targets --quiet: exit 0.
- Built-binary probe: outer init exit 0; init in outer/inner exit 4 naming the outer root with both remediation lines; init --nested exit 0 printing Root: <outer>/inner and creating inner/.beads/config.json with prefix inner.
- Pre-existing main red, NOT this bead (control-proven): publication_failure_splits_without_rollback_then_recovers fails identically on parent dd79a2d0 (control extraction /data/build/bead-rs/e4acee24-ctrl-src) - kept out of the close verified block; the other 10 tests in that suite pass. checkpoint_unknown_field_record_corpus / redaction_publication / redaction_storage / restore_export_unknown_field_conformance failures in earlier full runs also reproduce on the control.

issue.description:
ADR-005's acknowledged drawback: there is no way to record that an assigned open issue is a deliberate operator reservation, so legitimate parks trip the ready_frontier warning on every run and train operators to ignore it — the classic path to a warning losing its meaning. Work: add a first-class held/reserved marker settable via bead update, exclude marked issues from the ready_frontier warning while keeping them excluded from the claim frontier, carry the marker through checkpoint round trips and the unknown-field corpus, and document its interaction with reopen's assignee retention.
